core_obligations: Reduce to a comparison of resolutions (proof lines 1884-1900): the author reduces the statement to showing that an injective object of Mod(O) is acyclic as an abelian sheaf, so that an injective resolution in Mod(O) also computes cohomology in Ab(C).

Apply the vanishing criterion (proof lines 1903-1910): for an injective module I the author applies the companion vanishing criterion to obtain the vanishing of the abelian cohomology of I in positive degrees.

Conclude for all objects (proof lines 1913-1919): the case of a general object U, and the case where C has a final object giving the first displayed equality, follow from the same vanishing statement.
proof_roadmap: Show that an injective module is acyclic as an abelian sheaf, using the vanishing criterion of the section.
Conclude that an injective resolution in modules computes abelian cohomology.
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that the cohomology of a module over a sheaf of rings on a site agrees with the cohomology of its underlying abelian sheaf, both globally and over any object (statement lines 1861-1882). The proof reduces the comparison to the statement that an injective module is acyclic as an abelian sheaf (proof lines 1884-1900), which the author obtains from the vanishing criterion for cohomology over a cofinal system of coverings (proof lines 1903-1910), and then deduces both equalities, the global one requiring the case of a site with a final object (proof lines 1913-1919). The non-formal content is the acyclicity of injective modules viewed as abelian sheaves. The claim is H2: one reduction plus one criterion.
